new_statements.translation: Ocotepec Zoque (ZOCO) has a trochaic (strong-weak) stress pattern; it does not privilege bases or morphemes, and it is not sensitive to syllable weight, since [stressed] syllables may be light (CV) or heavy (CVC), as shown in (1). When words are monosyllabic, the only syllable carries the stress, as in (2). ... The trochaic pattern is assigned from right to left, as seen in trisyllabic words in (3) and four-syllable words in (4) [all with stress on the penultimate syllable].

new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the (morphologically complex) word: a single right-aligned, weight-insensitive trochee, counting suffixes and enclitics (e.g. =pə REL, -ʔam 'ya') as part of the stress domain; monosyllables are stressed. Faarlund 2012 (snippets) states the same rule ('regularly on the penultimate syllable.. regardless whether the stressed syllable belongs to the root or to a suffix or a clitic') and adds two morphophonological exceptions yielding final stress.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned by de la Cruz Morales 2023. Second-hand (Oxford Handbook of Language Prosody 2021 snippet, citing Herrera Zendejas 1993 and Faarlund 2012): secondary stress on every other syllable preceding the primary stress.
new_statements.exceptions: de la Cruz Morales: none. Faarlund 2012 (snippet only): (1) plural -yaj + dependent -e/i contracts to -yé, stressed even when word-final (mye'ché 'searching', chükyé 'making'); (2) plural -tam + -u contraction leaves stress on the a. Harrison & Harrison 1984: Spanish-loan compounds carry a written accent because they deviate; Zoque-Zoque compounds keep a main stress on each member.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the phonological word including suffixes and enclitics (examples (4a,b) show enclitic =pə and -ʔam counted for penult placement); examples are inflected verb forms and nouns in citation/utterance form from a text corpus.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement (de la Cruz Morales 2023) and Faarlund 2012 both describe the Ocotepec/Tapalapa variety ('zoque de Ocotepec', ZOCO; Faarlund: 'Ocotepec/Tapalapa variant of Chiapas Zoque'), which Glottolog files under rayo1235 Northeast/Rayón Zoque (ISO zor). Harrison & Harrison 1984 is the Rayón town variety proper; Herrera Zendejas 1995 describes Chapultenango Zoque, also within the zor area. All sources examined agree or are consistent with penultimate stress; no dialect-internal disagreement seen.

new_statements.quote: Los ejemplos de 8 indican dos aspectos importantes: por un lado, en todos los casos el acento se observa en la sílaba par, de derecha a izquierda, sea ésta una sílaba simple (8a), o bien contenga una rima compleja (8b); por otro lado, su ubicación no considera la composición morfológica de la palabra, pues ya se trate de derivación o de flexión, el acento siempre cae en el mismo lugar. Esto quiere decir que estamos frente a una lengua con acento fijo, en la cual los diferentes afijos no forman grupos en razón de si modifican o no el acento de la base, sea cual fuere el afijo, el acento se localiza en la penúltima sílaba. [p. 154] ... en ellos hay un acento principal en la penúltima sílaba y un acento secundario que alterna en las sílabas pares. [p. 156]
new_statements.translation: The examples in (8) show two important things: on the one hand, in every case the stress is observed on the even syllable counting from right to left, whether it is a simple syllable (8a) or contains a complex rime (8b); on the other hand, its placement takes no account of the morphological make-up of the word, for whether derivation or inflection is involved the stress always falls in the same place. This means we are dealing with a language with fixed stress, in which the various affixes do not form groups according to whether or not they modify the stress of the base; whatever the affix, the stress is located on the penultimate syllable. [p. 154] ... in them there is a primary stress on the penultimate syllable and a secondary stress alternating on the even syllables. [p. 156] (scanned of the PDF text layer reads 'mmfológica', 'ftjo', 'aftjo' for morfológica, fijo, afijo; corrected here against the printed page.)

new_statements.relation_note: Same placement as the catalog penultimate stress (penultimate) and as de la Cruz Morales 2023's trochaic weight-insensitive statement for Ocotepec; adds the secondary-stress pattern (alternating even syllables from the right, initial syllable of odd-count words unstressed, so a fuller word pattern would be 10, 010, 2010, 02010, 202010..), explicit weight-insensitivity (simple vs complex rime irrelevant), morphology-blindness (postlexical assignment), loanword re-stressing, and a formal metrical analysis. The data come from the Chapultenango variety, a sister town of Ocotepec within Wonderly's 'zoque del noroeste' (northeast Chiapas Zoque) group, not from Ocotepec itself (author states in fn…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress is fixed on the penultimate syllable of the word regardless of morphology (derivation, inflection, compounding) and regardless of syllable weight (CV and CVC rimes count alike); binary left-dominant (trochaic) feet are built from right to left, giving secondary stress on every other syllable to the left of the penult (4-syllable words: secondary on the first, e.g. kóketúmin 'escama'); in words with an odd number of syllables the leftover initial syllable forms a defective foot and is unstressed (yawásihk 'ejote', ehtekowína 'jefe de los danzantes'). Stress is assigned postlexically, after all morphology. Spanish loans are re-stressed on the penult (kostál > kóstal, ánima > aníma, p. 155). Author's parameter statement (18)-(19), pp. 157-158: constituents [+]bounded, left-dominant, rightmost foot is head of the word; build feet from the right, binary feet only.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Yes: secondary stress on alternating even syllables counting from the right (grave accent in her examples): kóketúmin 'escama', hó'mapáhsun 'calabaza maciza', tóme'áhu 'se acercó' (p. 155-156); in 3- and 5-syllable words the initial syllable is unstressed (defective foot): yawásihk, tu'tmáta, ehtísu, ehtekowína, yati'ahísu, masandihkómo (p. 156).
new_statements.exceptions: None stated for native vocabulary; monosyllables not discussed in this section. Spanish loans conform (re-stressed to penult, p. 155).
new_statements.identity_note: Herrera Zendejas 1995, printed p. 37 (PDF p. 39): 'Los datos del presente estudio provienen de la variante de Chapultenango, la cual corresponde al zoque del noroeste en la clasificación de Wonderly', the group that also contains Tapalapa, Ocotepec, Pantepec and San Bartolomé. So the work describes Chapultenango Zoque, a sister dialect of the catalog's Ocotepec variety within the same Northeast Chiapas Zoque languoid (rayo1235), not Ocotepec itself; fn. 24 (printed p. 106) says she had no contact with the Ocotepec dialect.
